films.title: HEADQUARTERS
films.description: Magenta Skateboards' 21.5-minute HEADQUARTERS opens the door on the company's skater-owned operation through a globe-spanning VX1000 team film. The first-party bill names 19 featured and introduced riders, while the film's independently indexed sections preserve 10 additional documented appearances for a complete 29-skater roster.
creditNotes: Magenta's official film page and upload identify 19 featured and introduced riders and credit Stéphane 'Feugs' Feugas with VX filming.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies HEADQUARTERS as a 22-minute 2026 full-length, indexes 29 skater appearances and preserves 24 additional production contributors.
The two credit groups keep Magenta's principal first-party bill distinct from 10 additional riders independently identified in the film's indexed sections.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite explicitly catalogs France, the United States and Brazil, names Paris as a location and Southbank in London as a featured spot. No narrower comprehensive itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: HEADQUARTERS presents Magenta's '103% skater owned and operated' identity as both a company portrait and an international team film. Its continued VX1000 aesthetic and simultaneous DVD release place the project in the physical-video tradition that has long shaped Magenta's output.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is dedicated HEADQUARTERS title artwork over the Paris skyline and contains no trailer, episode or event labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Magenta Skateboards' official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and supplies the 19-name featured bill and Stéphane Feugas filming credit. YouTube reports status OK, a 1,293-second runtime, channelId UCJuMDQgmBluqtdpk5DAA5JA and May 12, 2026 publication. Controlled Chrome measured 1,292.901 seconds at readyState 4 and the exact player advanced from 7.466 to 15.446 seconds without media error.
Magenta's first-party film page describes the project as a look inside its skater-owned headquarters, repeats the full featured roster, credits Feugs and links the physical DVD edition.

Independent filmography classifies HEADQUARTERS as a 22-minute 2026 full-length, catalogs 29 rider appearances and 24 production contributors, and identifies Paris, Southbank, France, the United States and Brazil.

films.title: WORKED
films.description: Pylon Skateboards' 14-minute WORKED connects Seattle, Los Angeles and Vancouver through five named soundtrack sections and an eight-skater first-party cast. The compact team film pairs Pylon regulars with Zoe Zollinger and preserves Paul Higgins as the independently cataloged production contributor.
creditNotes: Pylon's official upload bills eight cast members by their public handles; independent sources resolve @zoe_zollinger_ as Zoe Zollinger, @ninja__ginga__ as Caleb Nicholls and @notorious.t.a.c as Tshawn Cope.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies WORKED as a 14-minute 2026 full-length, identifies five named-section riders, catalogs seven of the eight first-party cast members and preserves Paul Higgins as a production contributor.

Zoe Zollinger is retained from Pylon's first-party cast even though the independent archive's current seven-name skater index omits her; The Boardr independently confirms her name, handle and Pylon sponsorship.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite explicitly catalogs Seattle, Los Angeles and Vancouver and identifies both United States and Canadian production geography.
films.historicalContext: Released with the dedication 'for everyone that got WORKED this year,' Pylon's concise 2026 full-length joins the company's Pacific Northwest base to scenes in Los Angeles and Vancouver while keeping the cast larger than its five named soundtrack sections.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is dedicated fluorescent-yellow WORKED title artwork over a Pylon skate image, with no trailer, episode or event labeling.

films.title: You Got It My Boy Jamie...
films.description: Polar Skate Co.'s 28.5-minute You Got It My Boy Jamie... grew from Jamie Platt footage into a full team film by Pontus Alv and Sirus F Gahan. The complete credits retain 13 upload-featured skaters, two named guests and two additional featured narrative appearances, alongside a 19-person filming roster and dedicated sound and music supervision credits.
additionalProductionCredits: Francis Peters — sound design and sound mix
creditNotes: Polar's official film page calls the release a film by Pontus Alv and Sirus F Gahan and names 12 principal team riders; the official upload expands the featured bill to include Hugo Håkannson and separately labels two guests and two additional featured appearances.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the release as a 28-minute full-length, catalogs all 17 skater appearances and preserves the five principal filmers, 14 additional camera contributors, sound designer and music supervisor.

Free Skate Mag independently documents the July 2 release and highlights Nathan Clancy and Jamie Platt; VHSMAG's Sirus Gahan/Jamie Platt interview explains the project's development and visual concept.
films.locationNote: VHSMAG's interview explicitly anchors Jamie Platt and Sirus F Gahan's long collaboration in Bournemouth and discusses a London-area ender and London production logistics. These are supported locations, not a claim of a complete global itinerary.
films.historicalContext: Polar framed the project as another full-length made less than two years after two prior company films, defending the format as a durable record of travel, friendship and shared sessions. Jamie Platt told VHSMAG that roughly 70 percent of his footage began as a Converse part before his move to Vans; that material became the foundation for a larger team film centered on his long collaboration with Sirus F Gahan.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is a dedicated night-sky title card reading YOU GOT IT MY BOY JAMIE... and contains no trailer, episode or event labeling.
